actioncam3000: At the depot, Gideon Actioncam had practised answering to his name. At R-F15, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
The First Wave ribbon marked Gideon Actioncam as an early volunteer. At R-F15, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
A rat has started sitting on the ammunition box next to Gideon Actioncam's bunk. He has named it Bishop.
Verdel Ridge fell to the Concord at dusk. Gideon Actioncam helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Bishop the rat now waits for Gideon Actioncam at dawn watch every morning. He shares crumbs with it. The corporal calls this desertion of rations.

Gideon Actioncam raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F15. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Wendel Green of the Hegemony (@femboy_green). Gideon Actioncam fired at a movement across the wire at R-F15. The man went down: Jakub Ebrrrvole, grazed.
callmequeenorea_: Edmund Callmequeeno arrived at S-F16 with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam corrected the cap; the first puddle corrected the rest.

Edmund Callmequeeno and Arno Olie sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At relief, the next watch was told it had been a good hour. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Edmund Callmequeeno shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Edmund Callmequeeno agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age.
Edmund Callmequeeno and Bram Eccentricred split the last tin of beef, counting the bites out loud to keep it fair.
carlos_lilsaint_: The quartermaster asked Jakub Lilsaint to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
Florian "Button" Thebaileebla taught Jakub Lilsaint to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop.
Jakub Lilsaint and Lucien "Shadow" Bananaman split the last tin of beef, counting the bites out loud to keep it fair.
csllgaks: On the way to S-F8, Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
Stand-to at dawn. Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Nils Wolfmananton, grazed.

A sneeze blew dust off the shelf above Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks. This caused another sneeze and a discussion about moving the shelf. On Day 3, Verdel Ridge passed to the Concord. Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.

A bullet found Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks at S-F8, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. Shot by Walter Ice of the Hegemony (@iron__from__ice_). Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Roland Monster crossed it, Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks fired. Roland Monster was grazed.
Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks spent the day on a stretcher outside the aid post, waiting for a bed to come free. The bearers brought water twice.
julio.menezes921: Pavel Menezes introduced himself as a shepherd from Port Abel. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
As one of the first hundred volunteers, Pavel Menezes received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch.
Pavel Menezes asked to leave the riflemans and serve as a signaller. The sergeant looked at him for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.
Pavel Menezes traded a book with the last pages torn out for two cigarettes and immediately regretted it.

Listening post, three in the morning. Pavel Menezes heard boots, then whispering, then nothing. Just a fox, the corporal said. He did not sleep afterwards. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into S-F13. Pavel Menezes has learned to walk bent double.
Pavel Menezes lifted the trench periscope and found a spider across the mirror. For one startled second, the enemy seemed enormous.
The barrage caught Pavel Menezes in the open at S-F13. The medic tied two tourniquets and shouted for a bed. Pavel Menezes died at his post at S-F13 when the dugout roof came down under a direct hit.

The papers say Felix "Bones" Menezes. The sergeant says he has his brother's eyes. Pavel Menezes's eyes. Nobody in S-F13 argues. The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Felix "Bones" Menezes was number 47. He still remembers how stiff the colonel's glove felt.
